Fyodor Dostoevsky, The Brothers Karamazov, translated by Constance Garnett.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/fyodor-dostoevsky/the-brothers-karamazov/constance-garnett

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Fyodor Dostoevsky, the author, died 1881 (Russia (original); country of origin for this text: UK (translation first published 1912 in London by translator Constance Garnett, British)).
- Constance Garnett, the translator, died 1946.

First publication of the text used: 1880 (SE colophon: 'The Brothers Karamazov was published in 1880'; translation 1912 (colophon)).

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1880, before 1931;
  a published work enters the United States public domain 95 years after
  publication, so this work entered it in 1975.
- Country of origin (Russia (original); country of origin for this text: UK (translation first published 1912 in London by translator Constance Garnett, British)): copyright there lasts for life plus 70 years
  after the death of the last surviving person named above. The last to die
  did so in 1946, so the work entered the public domain there on
  1 January 2017.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- Colophon states original 1880, translation 1912
- Wikidata Q991: Dostoevsky died 1881-02-09
- Wikidata Q2495818: Garnett died 1946-12-17
